text:
maria: pushed seq-weighted batching telemetry to prod this morning, seeing unexpected pad spikes and two OOMs :eyes:

maria: telemetry names: seq_weight, batch_padding_bytes, kv_cache_bytes, workspace_alloc_peak

dan: what changed in the scheduler? did you alter kernel switch or pad policy?

dan: also can you paste the OOM logs?

maria: here's the OOM snippet from host gpu-87:
```
[OOM] workspace_alloc failed: requested 923MB, available 780MB
batch_info: batch_len=18, avg_seq=512, seq_weight=12456, pad_bytes=198MB
kernel_switch: triggered -> kernel_v2 (cumulative_alloc + temp_scratch)
kv_cache_bytes=312MB
```

shawn: saw similar in canary yesterday. flamegraph points to kernel_v2 init copying per-request KV shadow -> duplicates KV pages during warmup :/ https://perf/reports/fg/2041239001

infra-bot: deploy 2041238888 successful to prod (maria/seq-weighted-metrics)

anya: two quick ideas: (1) defer kernel switch until post-batch if possible, (2) add a seq_weight cap to batch admission so one huge request can't blow up whole batch

leo: small scheduler patch I prototyped:
```
# scheduler config
max_cumulative_seq_weight=15000
per_request_estimate = max(seq_len, kv_estimate_bytes / 1024)
```

dan: nice. did you test pad waste reduction numbers?

maria: experiment results from A/B (1000 batches each):
- baseline: avg batch padding 42MB, pad waste 21%
- seq_weight cap=15000: avg padding 19MB, pad waste 9%
- memory peak per-gpu: baseline 2.1GB, capped 1.6GB
- incidents: baseline 3 OOMs/1000, capped 0 OOMs/1000 :thumbsup:
kv cache interaction: enabling kv prefetch increased workspace by ~12MB per active seq; combined with kernel switch warmup it trips the OOM

shawn: mitigation we can flip quickly: (A) enforce max_cumulative_seq_weight, (B) reclaim temp scratch buffers immediately after kernel init (reclaim_on_batch_complete=true)

anya: caution: reclaiming aggressively caused fragmentation in earlier runs. We may need to adjust slab sizes — try 256KB slabs instead of 1MB for small buffers to reduce internal waste.

leo: agreed. also adding a lightweight pad estimator at admission reduces batch growth velocity so the kernel switch warmup doesn't accumulate

dan: what about KV eviction policy? lazy eviction kept bytes around longer; maybe make kv cache evict on large-batch events

maria: plan: rollout cap + reclaim toggle as feature flag to 10% canary next hour, monitor workspace_alloc_peak and OOM rate. If stable, bump to 50% and then full. I'll add telemetry on per-batch kv_cache_bytes + kernel_state transitions.

maria: action items: @leo open PR for cap + estimator, @anya run slab-size benchmark, @shawn add flamegraph hook on kernel init, @dan monitor canary metrics. Will update in 30m.

shawn: :fire:

dan: :+1:

maria: thanks all — will post follow-up with canary dashboard link.
